items.headline: Scandal-hit Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang quits, plunging AI chipmaking giant into turmoil
items.blurb: US lawmakers now want to question him over whether one of his alleged relationships was with a Chinese spy.
items.text: Jensen Huang has abruptly quit as chief executive of AI chipmaking giant Nvidia after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs, in a stunning fall from grace that sent shockwaves from Silicon Valley to Capitol Hill. Nvidia is now under scrutiny from US lawmakers in Washington DC demanding Huang answer questions over whether one of his alleged relationships was with a Chinese spy. One of the world's most valuable companies as a result of the AI boom, Nvidia has lost $550bn (£415bn) in stock market value in just five days as the scandal dominated headlines. Nvidia's interim CEO, Colette Kress, called an emergency meeting of her executive team to discuss the company's future. His alleged conduct not only potentially crossed professional boundaries, but has made Nvidia the target of questions from US politicians who have expressed concern about national security risks. Huang, who has been Nvidia's public face since 1993, admitted on Sunday to having been "unfaithful" to his wife after reports he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, Alice Huang. items.headline: After Iraq ex-MP’s killing, Lebanon asks Syria to extradite suspects
items.blurb: Longtime Sunni politician and Iran critic was reportedly strangled in Beirut, sparking investigation.
items.text: Lebanese authorities have asked Syria to hand over two Syrians suspected of involvement in the killing of former Iraqi MP Ahmed al-Alwani, who was found dead in an apartment in Beirut earlier this week. A Lebanese judicial source told the AFP news agency that preliminary findings indicate al-Alwani was strangled to death, but the perpetrators and motives remain murky. Hailing from Ramadi in Iraq’s Sunni heartland, al-Alwani was a vocal critic of Iranian influence over Baghdad and had served more than a decade in prison after an initial death sentence on “terrorism” charges in his home country. Investigators at the Lebanese Public Prosecutor’s office had asked Damascus to arrest and hand over two Syrian nationals, the source added, who are suspected of involvement in al-Alwani’s killing. The source said the identities of the two suspects are yet to be determined, and that a Lebanese national had been arrested and is being interrogated. items.blurb: After a month-long investigation it was concluded that Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter, which won the £10,000 Caine prize, was ‘human-written’ The Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza has been cleared of using AI to write a prize-winning short story, after the prestigious Caine prize for African writers concluded…
items.text: After a month-long investigation it was concluded that Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter, which won the £10,000 Caine prize, was ‘human-written’ The Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza has been cleared of using AI to write a prize-winning short story, after the prestigious Caine prize for African writers concluded that his entry was “human-written” after a month-long investigation. Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter , which charts the declining fortunes of a family after the father invests in fish tanks, was announced as the winner of the £10,000 prize on 6 October. Five days later, the Atlantic published an article titled “Yet another literary prize winner seems to be AI”, in which the author and journalist Vauhini Vara said the AI-detection software Pangram, which itself uses AI, had deemed the story to be almost completely artificially generated. The Caine prize chair, Ellah Wakatama, said in a statement : “From our detailed investigation, we feel the evidence is clear: The Blue Fighter was human-written. We now look forward to awarding and celebrating Simbarashe Steyn Kundizeza … before the end of the year.” She said:

items.text: US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff held a fresh round of talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow, a day after the latest discussions aimed at ending the war in Ukraine wrapped up in Abu Dhabi. The pair are now in Dublin to meet Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky, and Witkoff said a new round of trilateral talks had already been agreed with Putin. But in a sign of further tension, Zelensky said on Thursday morning that Ukraine's military was again facing "systematic" restrictions to Starlink's military-grade satellite service, Starshield, meaning Kyiv was struggling to intercept Russian jet-powered drones. The peace talks in the Emirates were framed as being centred around European security arrangements in a post-war scenario, although a resolution to the war sparked by Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 still appears distant. items.headline: Albania’s PM says 2027 NATO summit will not be held in Tirana
items.blurb: Albania has faced criticism over low defence spending, as Rama is under pressure at home amid months of protests.
items.text: NATO will not be holding a summit in Albania next year as planned, Prime Minister Edi Rama has said, as his government faces criticism over its defence spending and protests at home. Speaking in Dublin on Thursday ahead of a gathering of European leaders, Rama said there was “not yet a common position on when the summit will happen, for sure not in 2027”. He added: “And in 2028, if it will be a summit, it will be in Tirana.” A NATO official said the next summit “will be held in Albania”, with a decision on the date yet to be made. Reuters reported in June that plans for a summit in Albania had been thrown into doubt by resistance from the administration of US President Donald Trump and dissatisfaction among NATO members with Tirana’s low defence spending. NATO leaders said in a declaration at their June 2025 summit in The Hague that they looked forward to meeting in Turkiye in 2026, “followed by a meeting in Albania”. The seven-time Formula One world champion has spoken out about conflict and humanitarian crises in the region, and has called for peace. He has frequently posted on social media about children killed in Israeli airstrikes in Gaza and called for a ceasefire. “I think we need to make sure we’re pushing to free Congo, free Sudan, free Syria, free Palestine . items.headline: Neither war nor peace in Tigray - is Ethiopia's latest conflict really over?
items.blurb: The army has taken control of most of Tigray's main towns - it is unclear if the TPLF is capable of fighting back.
items.text: Running a hair salon in Mekelle, capital of Ethiopia's troubled northern Tigray region, is not easy at the moment. "People can't prioritise beauty over daily basic needs. For many residents, thinking about self-care is a luxury, at a time when they can't feed their kids," Firut Me'ar, who runs a salon in the city, tells the BBC. After a brief war, the city is under the control of the national army but life is far from normal, says Firut, a single mother of a 10-year-old daughter. "Things are better than during the war, but people still have no money, no morale. Business is almost non-existent," she says, her voice shaking with emotion. Above all, she says people are worried about what the future holds. "There is uncertainty about what comes next." Fighting broke out in late September between the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), the party that had run Tigray for decades, and the national army - a resumption of the two-year civil war that officially ended in 2022. items.blurb: Saudi-led coalition intercepts flurry of suspected Houthi drones targeting oil and military infrastructure.
items.text: Saudi-led coalition forces have said they intercepted suspected Houthi drones over Saudi Arabia’s Riyadh region and Eastern Province, as the UN Security Council agreed to extend sanctions on the Iran-allied group. Major General Turki al-Maliki, the spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition, announced the interceptions of suspected Houthi drones on Thursday, in a statement carried by the Saudi Press Agency. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group had targeted oil infrastructure and military assets in the kingdom, including a pumping station on the East-West Pipeline with a drone as well as the Yanbu oil facility on the Red Sea. Riyadh says it has rerouted about 4 million barrels of crude per day via its East-West Pipeline to Yanbu, equivalent to about 4 percent of global supply. Saree further claimed a military cargo plane at Sharurah airport close to Yemen’s border was targeted with a drone, while a ballistic missile launched towards Khamis Mushait airbase “scored a direct hit”. items.headline: Collision of two trains in Egypt kills at least seven
items.blurb: President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said.
items.text: President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said. The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 50km (30 miles) south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry. An inspection indicated that the Cairo-Aswan train had been stationary on the same track, officials said. The health ministry gave the casualty toll, adding more than 70 of the injured were discharged after receiving treatment. Train derailments and crashes are common in Egypt, where the railway system has a history of mismanagement and poor maintenance of equipment. In recent years the government has announced modernisation initiatives to improve its railways. items.headline: Russian warship hit by Ukrainian drone in Gulf of Finland
items.blurb: The attack is thought to be the first time Ukrainian drones have attacked a Russian ship in an open stretch of the Baltic Sea.
items.text: Finnish officials have confirmed that a Russian warship was attacked in the Gulf of Finland on Wednesday, although little is known about the strike. Ukraine's SBU security service said it targeted the ship Naro-Fominsk as part of a broader drone operation against Russia's Ust-Luga oil export depot on the Baltic coast. The attack, thought to be the first time Ukrainian drones have attacked a Russian ship in an area of the Baltic Sea open to civilian maritime traffic, has raised questions about whether Ukraine could expand its strikes. Helsinki has been one of Kyiv's closest European allies, and Finnish officials have described the incident as a direct result of Russia's continued full-scale war. Finland's military has given few details of the incident, but it appears to have taken place in a narrow stretch some distance from the Finnish coast. The country's Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen was adamant that the situation in the Baltic Sea remained stable and safe and that there was no threat of any kind to marine traffic. items.headline: Crime Branch arrests Kerala Pravasi Association chief for alleged extortion attempt
items.blurb: The society reportedly received the notice on October 5, directing it to produce documents in connection with alleged financial irregularities, including money laundering
items.text: The Ernakulam District Crime Branch arrested Rajendran Vellapalath, chairman of the Kerala Pravasi Association, on Thursday for his alleged involvement in forging documents purportedly issued in the name of the Enforcement Directorate (ED) to extort money from a financial firm. He was arrested at Nedumbassery after he allegedly contacted the Indian Credit Cooperative Society in Thrissur, offering to settle an issue after the firm received a forged ED notice. The society reportedly received the notice on October 5, directing it to produce documents in connection with alleged financial irregularities, including money laundering. Shortly thereafter, the society received a call from Mr. Rajendran, who allegedly assured its representatives that he could settle the matter. However, the society contacted the ED’s zonal office in Delhi and learned that no such notice had been issued by the agency, following which it lodged a police complaint, said the police. items.headline: 57th IFFI to be held in Goa from Nov 20, adopts ‘Stories Without Borders’ theme
items.blurb: The theme emphasises cinema’s role in bridging cultural and geographical differences through diverse stories and shared human experiences
items.text: The 57th edition of the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) will be held in Goa from November 20 to 28. The festival will follow the theme “Stories Without Borders”, highlighting cinema’s ability to connect audiences across cultures and geographies. The festival’s highlights, key programmes and major attractions will be unveiled at a curtain-raiser press conference in Goa on Friday. Goa chief minister Pramod Sawant will attend the event along with secretary to the Union ministry of information and broadcasting Chanchal Kumar and chairperson of the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) G Krishnakumar. Filmmaker Ashutosh Gowariker, who is the festival director for the 2026 edition, will also be present. IFFI is one of the country’s major international film festivals which provides a platform for filmmakers from India and abroad to showcase their work and promote an understanding of different cultures through cinema. Its programme includes film screenings, retrospectives, workshops and discussions, encouraging cultural exchange among filmmakers and cinema enthusiasts. The 2026 edition is expected to feature a diverse selection of Indian and international films, reflecting the festival’s expanding global participation.

This comes days after the Diamond Harbour MP attacked the judiciary for dilly-dallying over a case related to his security downgrade after the BJP government came to power. “Ask your client. Who are the judges with the BJP? Please give the list. Your client is very intelligent as per the statement. Let your client give the list of those who belong to the BJP and those who belong to the AITC,” a bench of Justice Krishna Rao remarked. items.headline: Draft electoral rolls for SSR published in 13 states, 3 UTs; UP to release on Nov 17
items.blurb: Bihar’s list adds about 1.3 million electors over its post-SIR roll, while Tamil Nadu’s count rises to 57.7 million but remains below its pre-revision total.
items.text: Draft electoral rolls were published on Thursday in 16 states and Union territories as part of the Election Commission of India (ECI)’s Special Summary Revision (SSR) 2027, marking the start of a month-long window for claims and objections. Originally slated for 17 states and UTs with January 1, 2027, as the qualifying date, Thursday’s rollout covers 13 states —Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Manipur, Punjab, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Uttarakhand, West Bengal —and three UTs —Andaman & Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep and Puducherry — after Uttar Pradesh deferred its draft publication by five days to November 17. Voters across these regions have until December 11, 2026, to submit claims and objections ahead of the final roll publication on January 4, 2027. The window for UP voters will now run until December 16. The qualifying date is the cut-off by which a person must have turned 18 to be eligible for enrolment in a given revision. The company had reported total income of ₹104.09 crore and profit of ₹1.34 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year, according to a company statement. For the first half of FY27, NHC Foods posted total income of ₹821.45 crore, an increase of 282 per cent from ₹214.68 crore a year earlier. Profit rose nearly 13-fold to ₹38.68 crore, compared with ₹3.01 crore in the year-ago period. Commenting on the performance, Managing Director Satyam Joshi said, "We are encouraged by the strong performance this quarter and in the first half and remain focused on sustaining this growth momentum. Our strategy is centred on expanding our operations, strengthening our presence in the agri commodities and food processing sectors, and pursuing opportunities that complement our capabilities. items.headline: Microsoft outage drags on for five hours, disrupting Outlook, Teams and Copilot for thousands across US
items.blurb: Microsoft faced a major outage on Thursday, disrupting access to Outlook, Teams and Copilot for several hours. The disruption also affected connectors used by OpenAI and Anthropic, while the company worked to restore affected servers and gradually bring services back online.
items.text: On Thursday (local time), Microsoft struggled to restore access to some of its workplace software, roughly five hours after the outage began, saying that users might still be unable to connect to products such as its email and chat services. Bloomberg reported that the disruption affected services such as Outlook, Teams, and Copilot, the company's artificial intelligence (AI) service, for a significant part of the US workday. The tech giant's products are among the most widely used software across businesses, government agencies, and educational institutions. Reuters reported that as of 6:00 pm ET (3:30 am IST the following day), Microsoft was still working to restore the affected servers. The company said it had observed limited recovery, with several users gradually able to reconnect. Reports of Outlook problems peaked at around 1:00 pm ET, reaching 138,058, before falling to approximately 34,490 by the evening, according to Downdetector. Earlier on Thursday, Microsoft attributed the disruption to several servers becoming unexpectedly unavailable under increased load, rather than a surge in traffic. This is a tricky debate with so many variables and a timescale as old as the game itself and, to my mind, not merely a determination of a player's individual ability but also a measure of their impact upon the nation's psyche. Ballon d'Or winners Stanley Matthews, Kevin Keegan and Michael Owen would surely have a shout if the criteria was such, not to mention genius technicians such as Glenn Hoddle, Chris Waddle and John Barnes. Likewise, if any England boss managed to extract the best from Paul Scholes, Steven Gerrard and Frank Lampard they would be surely making a classic late dart from midfield. Girish Rao, vice president of information technology at Lubrizol, says the company is building a digital foundation that connects business processes, modern data platforms, and cloud infrastructure to support its research and development (R&D) teams. items.blurb: Representatives from Nvidia told Illinois representative Bill Foster that it would be technically possible to implement the anti-smuggling measures called for in the Chip Security Act, Foster told MIT Technology Review in an interview on Thursday, even while an industry group claimed they were “potentially…
items.text: Representatives from Nvidia told Illinois representative Bill Foster that it would be technically possible to implement the anti-smuggling measures called for in the Chip Security Act, Foster told MIT Technology Review in an interview on Thursday, even while an industry group claimed they were “potentially infeasible.” Foster, a Democrat who serves on the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, is a cosponsor of the act, which would introduce geotracking requirements to verify the location of advanced AI chips in order to prevent their smuggling to China. It is one of three chip-security bills under consideration for inclusion in the Senate’s National Defense Authorization Act, each of which is drawing renewed attention after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation and reported affair with an alleged Chinese spy. When the Chip Security Act was introduced, in May 2025, lawmakers said the technology to implement it existed, something Nvidia has not publicly confirmed. In March 2026, the Semiconductor Industry Association, of which Nvidia is a member, explicitly opposed the bill and wrote that its mandates for chip tracking were “new, untested, and potentially infeasible.”

items.text: Democrats on Thursday opened an inquiry into how the Trump administration handled Nvidia’s chip sales to China. Earlier on Thursday, the company ousted its CEO Jensen Huang . He also agreed to testify to a different set of Republican-led Congressional committees. Huang was removed from the company he founded after he confessed to an extramarital affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy. (He has since been accused of having more affairs , with Nvidia employees.) The alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang, was an executive of Nvidia customer Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that U.S. officials suspect of helping route advanced Nvidia chips into China. The Democratic inquiry comes from Rep. Richard Neal (D-Mass.), the top Democrat on the House Ways and Means Committee, and Sen. Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), the top Democrat on the Senate Finance Committee. As the minority party, they can ask questions but can’t compel answers. items.headline: Google faces calls for AI moratoriums in schools after Gemini pilot backlash
items.blurb: Families confront Google after teen’s lawsuit labels Gemini a “suicide coach.”
items.text: CHICAGO—Families joined protests in seven cities nationwide on Wednesday, rallying against what they see as Google’s bid to entrench its AI models in schools, turn kids of all ages into Gemini guinea pigs, and hook them on AI. The backlash follows a Google statement last week, confirming that there will be no way for students to use Google Search without AI. While Google claimed it was giving schools “more choice, not less”—by turning off Search, Gemini, and Gemini Notebook by default—it would not provide an option that allowed Search without AI. For students, the only way to avoid interacting with AI was to remember to add “-ai” to every query, parents worried. In Chicago, many families showed up to protest Google, despite cold, rainy weather. Waving signs, dozens of protesters marched up to Google’s downtown office as workers seemed to be leaving for the day, shouting chants like “Hey Google, nice try, we don’t want your Gemini” and “Hey, Google, leave our kids alone!” Called to action by a nonprofit grassroots advocacy group, the Illinois Families for Public Schools (ILFPS),

items.text: As a California state senator, Scott Wiener authored legislation aimed at curbing the risks of advanced AI. Now, after winning a tight congressional race for former Speaker of the House Nancy Pelosi’s open San Francisco seat, he could play a key role in setting federal AI policy. I spoke with Wiener on Friday, only a few hours after he had been declared the victor. But he was already thinking about AI risk. The previous day, the AI nonprofit METR had released a report that had been widely interpreted as evidence that Anthropic had achieved recursive self-improvement, a phenomenon in which AI meaningfully contributes to its own advancement and AI progress potentially spins out of control. “It’s very concerning,” Wiener said, citing the report as evidence that we are quickly running out of time to regulate AI. “It was my hope that Congress would take decisive action before the end of this year,” he said. “That does not appear to be happening.” Wiener has been increasingly focused on AI in recent years, and he’s made many of the AI safety movement’s

items.text: Zupee has laid off its entire workforce and is on the verge of shutting down operations, weeks after announcing an AI pivot. The developments raise questions about whether the AI pivot was a genuine business transition or an attempt to mask the impending shutdown, and what happens to the nearly $120 Mn raised by the startup. Zupee has discontinued its gaming operations, shut down NeoAstro and Zupee Studio, while its proposed acquisition of microdrama startup Vertical TV also fell through. Delhi NCR-based gaming startup Zupee has nothing more to lose. For one, it has laid off its entire workforce. Then, its announcement of a pivot towards AI has failed to see the light of day. According to sources, the startup has provided severance pay to the affected employees, covering the period until January 2027, and its October pivot was a veiled attempt to present the impending closure. The final round of layoffs coincided with Zupee’s public announcement of its foray into AI, Inc42 has learnt. OpenAI Brings API Inference Residency To India To Deepen Enterprise AI Adoption
items.blurb: ChatGPT maker OpenAI has introduced local inference and data processing for its APIs in India, adding to its efforts to…
items.text: ChatGPT maker OpenAI has introduced API inference residency in India, allowing eligible businesses to process supported GPT-6 Luna workloads within the country The move addresses data localisation requirements that have been a barrier to AI adoption among regulated businesses and increases competition for Indian AI companies offering locally hosted models Details: The service supports GPT-6 Luna through the Responses and Chat Completions APIs, with both processing and supported customer data storage taking place in India ChatGPT maker OpenAI has introduced local inference and data processing for its APIs in India, adding to its efforts to expand the commercialisation of ChatGPT in its largest market. For context, local data inferencing allows businesses to ensure that both API requests and the computing required to generate responses take place within India for supported workloads. It is initially available for the GPT-6 Luna model and extends OpenAI’s existing data residency options in the country.
